memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Yet the Lord says, 'During the forty years that I led you through the wilderness, your clothes did not wear out, nor did the sandals on your feet. You ate no bread and drank no wine or other fermented drink. I did this so that you might know that I am the Lord your God.'" — Deut 29:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Look at the quiet, faithful care of God over forty years in the wilderness. Their clothes did not wear out. Their sandals held together. Though they had no fields to farm or vineyards to tend, God fed them with manna and gave them water. Day after day, year after year, He sustained them — and He tells them why: "so that you might know that I am the Lord your God."

God's provision was not just about survival; it was about relationship. He wanted them to know Him, to learn through daily dependence that He is faithful. Every unworn sandal was a quiet sermon: I am with you. I will provide. I am the Lord your God.

We often overlook God's ongoing, everyday faithfulness. We notice the dramatic answers to prayer but miss the countless quiet provisions — the daily bread, the strength for another day, the small mercies that hold our lives together. Yet these too are God saying, "Know that I am the Lord your God."

Jesus reminds us that our Father knows our needs and clothes even the grass of the field (Matt 6:30-32). If God sustained a whole nation in a barren desert for forty years, He can be trusted with your needs today. Look for His quiet, faithful care in the ordinary things, and let it deepen your knowledge of Him. He is providing more than you realise.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do I see God's quiet, everyday faithfulness in my life?
2. Am I learning to know God through my daily dependence on Him?
3. What "unworn sandal" — a small, steady mercy — can I thank God for today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful God, thank You for sustaining me in ways I often overlook. Open my eyes to Your quiet, daily care, and through it help me know You more deeply as my Lord. Amen.
